primary_report.scope: Heavy-Walsh rotated rank-three indefinite family bounded by 4 sqrt(2e), plus a same-family obstruction to best-principal-triple determinant/pivot selection.

partner_result_applied.applied_equation: density caps for disjoint null factors -> saddle half-potential <=4 sqrt(e); dependence-safe Abel smoothing then gives ||p_Q||_infinity<=4 sqrt(e/c)<=4 sqrt(2e)

other_dependency.scope_applied: rank-one specialization of Fourier--Brascamp--Lieb gives density cap sqrt(e) for normalized linear forms with maximum coefficient square <=1/2

new_theorem.statement_compact: For the heavy-Walsh frame U with c in [1/2,1), A=U diag(1,1,-1)U^T and its negative have density sup at most 4 sqrt(2e) for every independent marginal density cap one.
new_theorem.rank_two_control: Deleting the third square leaves a product of two independent null factors whose density is logarithmically singular at zero for uniform original inputs.
new_theorem.third_direction_mechanism: The rank-two product has a uniform one-sided half-potential; the overlapping third square is a conditional translate mixture of an untouched independent heavy coordinate and its Abel kernel consumes that half-potential.

new_strategy_falsifier.claim_refuted: A universal global proof can select one best physical principal 3x3 block and apply a determinant/pivot local density estimate.
new_strategy_falsifier.family_behavior: For fixed c, max_{I,k}|A_kk det A[I,I]|^(1/4) tends to zero as m tends to infinity while the global density remains <=4 sqrt(2e).

unresolved_implication: Develop an aggregated heavy/diffuse mechanism for arbitrary rotated exact-rank-three frames: either a quantitative null-factor decomposition/product-projection bound after a heavy row, or a diffuse Brascamp--Lieb chart after heavy-coordinate removal. Arbitrary full-rank matrices additionally retain nonseparable residual-spectrum debt.
next_step: Stress arbitrary heavy-row 3-frames by optimizing null directions in the 2D opposite-sign plane and test whether disjoint-support splitting can be replaced by a Brascamp--Lieb/Rogozin projection-density bound strong enough for the partner half-potential estimate.
